items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: The interviewee (Mickey Roker) does not mention Ramsey Lewis; the interviewer mentions playing behind Ramsey Lewis, and the interviewee responds generally about drummers and showmanship without referencing a personal connection to Lewis.

ctx.x: Well the way I solo I keep the melody in mind. I always sing the melody. See drummers make great singers because they don’t get changes to play, so they’ve got to keep the melody in mind. And if you do that, you can put, the rhythm is so infinite man that there’s so much you can do. But when people listen to a drummer play they want energy man, they want dynamics, they want the same thing that the drummer wants. It’s up to the guy taking the solo to sell himself to the people that’s listening you know. It’s up to…

You know I had a chance, I was playing in a orchestra. I was playing the string bass in the string section behind Ramsey Lewis one night. And his drummer was basically saying he realized he was not a power drummer. So he got his excitement, he played a chorus and about every eight measures he got softer and softer and softer. He said “no I’m not going to overpower this drumset. I’m going to do it just exact opposite way. I’m going to give you things you don’t expect. You don’t expect the drums to be soft.” So he…
out pretty good, and then every eight measures he got softer. He went down to brushes. Finally he put the brushes down and said “Just beat on the chest.”
